The most recent **medical guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of hypertension** are primarily based on recommendations from major health organizations, including the **American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA), European Society of Cardiology (ESC), and the International Society of Hypertension (ISH)**. Below is a summary of the latest guidelines (as of mid-2024):

---

### **1. Diagnosis of Hypertension**
#### **Blood Pressure (BP) Classification (ACC/AHA 2017, ESC 2023, ISH 2020)**
| Category | Systolic BP (mmHg) | Diastolic BP (mmHg) | Management Recommendation |
|----------|-------------------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| **Normal** | <120 | **and** | <80 | Lifestyle optimization |
| **Elevated** | 120–129 | **and** | <80 | Lifestyle changes |
| **Stage 1 Hypertension** | 130–139 | **or** | 80–89 | Lifestyle + consider meds if high-risk (e.g., CVD, diabetes, CKD) |
| **Stage 2 Hypertension** | ≥140 | **or** | ≥90 | Lifestyle + **pharmacotherapy** |
| **Severe Hypertension (Hypertensive Crisis)** | ≥180 | **and/or** | ≥120 | **Immediate treatment** (hospital if symptomatic) |

#### **Key Diagnostic Recommendations (ESC 2023, ACC/AHA 2023 Updates)**
- **Out-of-office BP measurement** (ambulatory BP monitoring **ABPM** or home BP monitoring **HBPM**) is **strongly recommended** to confirm hypertension (avoids "white-coat" or "masked" hypertension).
  - **ABPM (24-hour):**
    - **Daytime avg:** ≥135/85 mmHg
    - **Nighttime avg:** ≥120/70 mmHg
    - **24-hour avg:** ≥130/80 mmHg
  - **HBPM:** Avg ≥135/85 mmHg (based on multiple readings)
- **Automated office BP (AOBP)** is preferred over manual measurements to reduce observer bias.
- **Secondary hypertension** should be suspected in:
  - Resistant hypertension (BP remains ≥130/80 despite ≥3 meds, including a diuretic)
  - Sudden onset (<30 or >55 years)
  - Hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis (suggests **primary aldosteronism**)
  - Abdominal bruit (renal artery stenosis)
  - Flank masse, proteinuria (renal parenchymal disease)
  - Headaches, palpitations, sweating (pheochromocytoma)
  - Truncal obesity, striae (Cushing’s syndrome)

---

### **2. Risk Stratification (ESC 2023, ACC/AHA 2023)**
- **CV risk assessment** is crucial for determining treatment intensity.
- **ESC uses SCORE2** (for Europe) or **ASCVD Risk Calculator** (US) to estimate 10-year CVD risk.
- **High-risk patients** (e.g., diabetes, CKD, established CVD, or 10-year risk ≥10%) should start **medications earlier** (even at Stage 1 hypertension).

---

### **3. Treatment Goals (BP Targets)**
#### **General Population (ESC 2023, ACC/AHA 2023)**
| Patient Group | Systolic BP Target | Diastolic BP Target |
|--------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **General (low-moderate risk, <65 years)** | **<130** | **<80** |
| **General (high risk or ≥65 years)** | **<130** (if tolerated) | **<80** |
| **Diabetes Mellitus** | **<130** | **<80** |
| **Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)** | **<130** | **<80** (with albuminuria) |
| **Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)** | **<130** | **<80** |
| **Stroke/TIA** | **<130** | **<80** (if stable) |
| **Frail Elderly (>80 years)** | **<150** (or **<130** if tolerated) | **<90** |

- **ESC 2023** emphasizes **personalized targets** based on tolerability.
- **ACC/AHA 2023** maintains **<130/80** for most patients, but allows **<150/90** in very elderly if frail.

---

### **4. Lifestyle Modifications (First-Line for All Patients)**
- **Dietary Approaches:**
  - **DASH diet** (rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy, reduced sodium).
  - **Sodium restriction:** <1.5 g/day (ideal) or at least **<2.3 g/day** (5 g salt).
  - **Potassium-rich foods** (unless CKD or on ACEi/ARB + potassium-sparing diuretics).
  - **Limit alcohol:** ≤1 drink/day for women, ≤2 for men.
- **Physical Activity:**
  - **Aerobic exercise:** 90–150 min/week (e.g., brisk walking, cycling).
  - **Resistance training:** 2–3 sessions/week.
- **Weight Management:**
  - **BMI <25 kg/m²** (even 5–10 kg loss can lower BP).
- **Smoking Cessation & Stress Reduction** (yoga, meditation).

---

### **5. Pharmacological Treatment (Stepwise Approach)**
#### **First-Line Antihypertensives (ESC 2023, ACC/AHA 2023)**
- **Initial Therapy (Monotherapy or Combination):**
  - **ACE Inhibitors (ACEi)** (e.g., lisinopril, ramipril) or **ARBs** (e.g., losartan, valsartan) – **preferred in diabetes, CKD, or HF**.
  - **Calcium Channel Blockers (CCBs)** (e.g., amlodipine, felodipine) – good for elderly or isolated systolic HTN.
  - **Thiazide-like Diuretics** (e.g., **chlorthalidone > hydrochlorothiazide**, indapamide) – effective for volume-dependent HTN.
  - **Beta-blockers** (e.g., metoprolol, nebivolol) – **only if compelling indication** (e.g., CAD, HF, arrhythmias).

- **Recommended Initial Combinations (for Stage 2 HTN or high-risk patients):**
  - **ACEi/ARB + CCB** (e.g., amlodipine + valsartan)
  - **ACEi/ARB + Thiazide-like diuretic** (e.g., lisinopril + chlorthalidone)
  - **CCB + Thiazide-like diuretic** (e.g., amlodipine + indapamide)

- **Resistant Hypertension (BP remains uncontrolled on ≥3 drugs):**
  - **Add spironolactone (aldosterone antagonist)** (25–50 mg/day) – **most effective 4th-line agent**.
  - **Other options:** Beta-blocker, clonidine, or **SGLT2 inhibitors** (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) – emerging evidence for BP lowering in CKD/diabetes.
  - **Consider secondary causes** (renal artery stenosis, primary aldosteronism, OSA).

#### **Special Populations:**
| Condition | Preferred Agents | Avoid |
|-----------|------------------|-------|
| **Pregnancy** | Labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa | ACEi, ARBs, aliskiren |
| **Diabetes** | ACEi/ARB ± CCB/diuretic | Beta-blockers (if not compelling) |
| **CKD (Proteinuria)** | ACEi/ARB (renoprotective) | NSAIDs, dual RAAS blockade |
| **Heart Failure (HFrEF)** | ACEi/ARB + Beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2i | CCBs (non-DHP), thiazides (if GFR <30) |
| **Atrial Fibrillation** | Beta-blocker or CCB (rate control) | - |
| **Black Patients** | CCB + Thiazide (better BP response) | ACEi/ARB alone (less effective as monotherapy) |

---

### **6. Follow-Up & Monitoring**
- **After starting treatment:**
  - Recheck BP **within 1 month** (sooner if severe HTN).
  - Titrate doses or add drugs every **4–6 weeks** until target achieved.
- **Long-term monitoring:**
  - Every **3–6 months** if stable.
  - Annual **labs** (electrolytes, creatinine, glucose, lipid panel).
- **Home BP monitoring** encouraged for better adherence.

---

### **7. Emerging & Controversial Topics (2023–2024 Updates)**
- **BP Targets in Very Elderly (>80 years):**
  - **ESC 2023** allows **<150 systolic** if frail, but **<130 if tolerated**.
  - **STEP Trial (2021)** showed benefits of **intensive BP control (110–130) even in octogenarians**.
- **SGLT2 Inhibitors & GLP-1 Agonists:**
  - **Dapagliflozin, empagliflozin** lower BP and reduce CV events in **diabetes/CKD**.
  - **Semaglutide** may have modest BP-lowering effects.
- **Device-Based Therapies:**
  - **Renal Denervation (RDN):** Now **FDA-approved (2023)** for resistant HTN (e.g., **Medtronic’s Symplicity Spyral**).
  - **Baroreceptor Activation Therapy (BAT)** – investigational.
- **AI & Digital Health:**
  - **Wearable BP monitors** (e.g., Omron HeartGuide) and **AI-driven risk prediction** are being integrated.

---

### **8. Key Guideline References**
| Organization | Latest Guideline | Year | Key Focus |
|-------------|------------------|------|-----------|
| **ESC/ESH** | [2023 ESC Guidelines on Hypertension](https://www.escardio.org/Guidelines/Clinical-Practice-Guidelines/Hypertension) | 2023 | Personalized BP targets, emphasis on ABPM, combination therapy |
| **ACC/AHA** | [2023 AHA/ACC Hypertension Guideline Update](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/HYP.0000000000000231) | 2023 | Maintains <130/80, new data on SGLT2i, RDN |
| **ISH (Global)** | [2020 ISH Global Guidelines](https://ish-world.com/publications/global-guidelines/) | 2020 | Low-resource settings, simplified algorithms |
| **NICE (UK)** | [NG136 Hypertension in Adults](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng136) | 2019 (Updated 2023) | ABPM for diagnosis, <135/85 target for HBPM |

---

### **Summary of Key Takeaways (2024)**
✅ **Diagnose with ABPM/HBPM** (not just office BP).
✅ **Target BP <130/80 for most**, <150/90 in frail elderly if needed.
✅ **Lifestyle changes first**, then **combination therapy** (ACEi/ARB + CCB or thiazide).
✅ **Spironolactone for resistant HTN**.
✅ **SGLT2 inhibitors & RDN** are emerging options.
✅ **Personalize treatment** based on comorbidities (diabetes, CKD, HF).

Would you like a more detailed breakdown on any specific aspect (e.g., resistant HTN, pregnancy, or new drugs)?
